newsitem.title: BELGIUM: S.Africa will not send troops to 'war' in Zaire - Mbeki.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa will not send troops to 'war' in Zaire - Mbeki.

text.p: South African Vice President Thabo Mbeki said on Thursday that his country was not prepared to send troops to Zaire to fight a war.
"There must be no shooting ...it is first important for a ceasefire to hold," Mbeki told a news conference during a visit to Belgium. "We wouldn't want to send troops to fight a war."
Mbeki said South Africa was still involved in international negotiations to seek a solution to the crisis in Central Africa, but would not commit a force until a mandate was agreed.
"We would prefer a relatively limited number of people to be involved," he said. "Ideally they should be involved in security and distribution."

The United Nations is currently trying to negotiate with Rwanda and Zaire for a mandate for an international force to help distribute aid to hundreds of thousands of refugees trapped in fighting in the region.
Zaire's army is battling Rwandan-backed Tutsi rebels who are pursuing former Hutu soldiers of the Rwanda armed forces mixed with refugees from the 1994 Rwandan civil war.
Mbeki said the sort of mandate that South Africa wanted to see given to any force would involve securing airports and guarding the storage and distribution of food aid.
"But the belligerants must first have agreed to stop fighting," he said. "We do not want to hunt down people who are armed ... (rather) participate in a political settlement.
Mbeki's comments echo those of Canada and the U.S. which are expected to land a contingent in Zaire within days.

Aid workers in Zaire, however, say that without taking on the thousands of armed Hutus, who are accused by the rebels of using refugees as human shields, the mission would be a failure as it will not lead to mass repatriation.
U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said Africa-bound U.S. troops would be armed to protect themselves but not to conduct combat operations while helping deliver aid to the refugees.
"We are not planning a mission to go in and disarm factions or to separate the military from refugees," he said.
Canada said on Thursday Lieutenant-General Maurice Baril would head the force. An advance team of Canadian troops was to leave for Zaire later on Thursday to assess the situation.
